# Implementing an aspect for a record

[Three forms](#spec.types.generics.row-conditional-impls.legality-1), with different rules:

```metel
extend { x: f64, y: f64 }: MyAspect { … }                    // one concrete row
extend<record R: .{ .x: f64, .. }> .{ ..R }: MyAspect { … }         // every row of a given shape
extend<record R> .{ ..R }: MyAspect { … }                         // every row
```

[All three are permitted once the aspect is local to the implementing module](#spec.types.generics.row-conditional-impls.legality-1): the first is
exactly one structural type, the others a *row condition* on the receiver. The receiver
matches an impl when its row meets the condition, whether it is an anonymous record or a
nominal [`record`](../../declarations/records.md). Methods are checked per call against the
concrete receiver, as for every structural target, and the aspect's default methods are
inherited as for any impl. The field types a target writes must be spelled out: one that
names an impl type parameter (`extend<T> .{ .w: T }: A`) is rejected, since no receiver's
field type could equal it.

The second also needs overlap checking between row bounds — two shape-conditional
implementations can be *incomparable* rather than one being more specific, so they must
be disjoint, which is specified below. The third is most useful with a way to require an
aspect of every field in the row ([Field-wise row
constraints](field-wise-row-constraints.md) above, `..R: Aspect`), which a record-target
impl accepts as `where ..R: Aspect`. The standard library implements `Display` for every record of `Display` fields this way
(its body is a built-in) and `Copy` for every record of `Copy` fields (a
bodyless impl): such a record is copied, not moved.

Two shape-conditional impls are disjoint when some label one requires the other forbids:

```metel
aspect Describe { fun describe(&self) -> String; }

extend<record R: .{ .name: String, .. }> .{ ..R }: Describe {
    fun describe(&self) -> String { "named ${self.name}" }
}
extend<record R: !{ .name }> .{ ..R }: Describe {
    fun describe(&self) -> String { "anonymous" }
}

fun main() {
    assert(.{ .name = "ada", .age = 36 }.describe() == "named ada");
    assert(.{ .age = 36 }.describe() == "anonymous");
}
```

The impl is chosen from the value's *current* row, so a partial move changes it:

```metel
record Handle { id: i64, name: String }

aspect Describe { fun state(&self) -> String; }

extend<record R: !{ .name }> .{ ..R }: Describe {
    fun state(&self) -> String { "no name" }
}
extend<record R: .{ .name: String, .. }> .{ ..R }: Describe {
    fun state(&self) -> String { "has name" }
}

fun main() {
    var h := Handle(id = 1, name = "secret");
    assert(h.state() == "has name");
    let name := h.name;                 // h : Handle.{ .id }
    assert(h.state() == "no name");
    assert(name == "secret");
}
```

[Two impls whose conditions do not exclude each other overlap and are rejected with
`T0015`](#spec.types.generics.row-conditional-impls.legality-3):

<!-- doc-example: expect-fail reason="two row-conditional impls that can both match overlap -- T0015 is the point" -->
```metel
aspect Describe { fun describe(&self) -> String; }

extend<record R: .{ .name: String, .. }> .{ ..R }: Describe {
    fun describe(&self) -> String { "a" }
}
extend<record R: .{ .id: i64, .. }> .{ ..R }: Describe {
    fun describe(&self) -> String { "b" }
}
```

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.types.generics.row-conditional-impls.legality-1}

A row-conditional impl (`extend<record R: .{ ... }> .{ ..R }: Aspect` or `extend<record R>
.{ ..R }: Aspect`) resolves against a value's **current** row, not only its widest
possible one — for a struct, that is the row of its current residual (narrower after a
partial move, wider again after the moved field is restored), exactly the same
current-row behavior [Named Records](../../declarations/records.md) states for `record`'s own
row-bound satisfaction.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.types.generics.row-conditional-impls.legality-2}

When a value's brand has an ordinary (brand-keyed) impl of an aspect and its row also
satisfies a row-conditional impl of the same aspect, the brand-keyed impl is selected:
brand-exact dispatch is checked first, and a match there short-circuits row-conditional
resolution entirely rather than conflicting with it.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.types.generics.row-conditional-impls.legality-3}

Two row-conditional impls of the same aspect do not conflict when some field name both
conditions mention is required present by one and absent (or incompatibly typed) by the
other — rows being open means no other fact can correlate two row conditions, so this
is the only way two of them can be proven disjoint. Any other pair of row-conditional
impls of the same aspect overlaps, and is rejected exactly as two overlapping ordinary
impls are. Inside a generic body over an unconstrained `<record R>`, a row-conditional
method is not visible unless `R`'s own bound entails the impl's condition.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->
